nodes.label: C1: Compressor/Diffuser/Thrust Mass-Flow Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Impeller b2=2.9 mm vs diffuser channel 7.0 mm (ratio 2.4 vs 1.0-1.15 rule); 176.5 N needs ~0.41 kg/s but b2=2.9 passes ~0.14 kg/s (needs ~8.7 mm). b2 was derived from the intake shell intersection at r=37, so measure the real wheel first; if real, cut diffuser height to ~3.0-3.2 mm and expect about half the thrust.

nodes.label: Simulated Design Point (176.5 N)
nodes.rationale: At compressor efficiency 0.72: PR 3.20, 0.412 kg/s air, TIT 800 C, EGT 662 C, methane 6.26 g/s (313 kW fuel); NGV unchoked (M 0.83), turbine loading 1.17. Only a theoretical ceiling until C1 is resolved.

nodes.label: I1: v12 Interference Check Incomplete
nodes.rationale: verify_pair.log stops after the bearing pairs and run1 was killed (exit 143); helical-thread booleans made checks too slow, so diffuser, CC, NGV, exhaust and casing were not pair-checked.

nodes.label: I2: Intake Outer M3 Thread Engagement FAIL
nodes.norm_label: i2: intake outer m3 thread engagement fail
nodes.rationale: 1.9 mm (0.63d) engagement at PCD82 fails the script's own check; use through-bolts with nuts or a thicker local boss.

nodes.label: I4: Misleading NGV Angle in README
nodes.norm_label: i4: misleading ngv angle in readme
nodes.rationale: README's 68/64 deg is an assumed camber angle; the effective exit angle from the measured throat is 58.9 deg, and the 1212 mm2 throat area is the matching criterion.

nodes.label: I6: Gas Supply Needs Booster or CNG
nodes.norm_label: i6: gas supply needs booster or cng
nodes.rationale: Full load needs ~31 Nm3/h methane at >=3 barg, while city gas is typically tens of mbar.

nodes.label: Compressor Wheel (Schwitzer 316954, turned down)
nodes.rationale: OD 74, inducer 55.9, exit width 2.9, 7 main + 7 splitter blades; twist/sweep (wrap 37 deg, backswept exit) taken from photos because no angle was given in any file.

nodes.label: Diffuser (Pos 4, aluminium)
nodes.rationale: Some vane geometry reconstructed from the front view; v8 added a 74.4-76 mm rim relief 0.5 deep so the compressor back gap stays 0.5.

nodes.label: Exhaust Duct (SS 0.5)
nodes.rationale: Inner cone moved to x=122.5 following the GR130 note of 1-2 mm to the turbine.

nodes.label: Front Bearing (sliding outer ring)
nodes.rationale: Front housing H6/H7 with a sliding outer ring (0.002-0.008 mm clearance) so the wave spring can preload it; v12 moved it to x2.1-9.1.

nodes.label: Front Bearing O-ring (22x1.0 FKM 75)
nodes.rationale: Gland 23.6 x1.4 with 20% squeeze and 70% fill; no rear O-ring because temperature exceeds the FKM limit and the rear bearing must slide for thermal growth.

nodes.label: GR180-3D FreeCAD Model
nodes.rationale: Parametric FreeCAD model of the GR180 shaft, shaft tunnel, diffuser and the full engine, rebuilt from one script; all dimensions in mm with the axial origin at the tunnel front face.

nodes.label: Spark Plug Igniter 1/4-32 UNEF
nodes.rationale: Placed at x=33.6 (12 mm behind the cap face) because liner hole rows forbid 5-8 mm; gap at r44 midway between two vaporisers.

nodes.label: Natural Gas (Methane) Fuel System, 4 barg
nodes.rationale: Estimated 176.5 N thrust and TSFC ~0.147 kg/N/h give methane ~6.2 g/s (~33 Nm3/h) at full power; 12 needles 1.5x0.2 run near-choked at ~3 barg manifold; 8 mm radial feed used because the 3 mm vane lines would choke at ~1.5 g/s.

nodes.label: Front Oil Jet (0.5 mm at 42 deg)
nodes.norm_label: front oil jet (0.5 mm at 42 deg)

nodes.label: Shaft Tunnel
nodes.rationale: 2 mm front spigot removed and flange face set to x=+0.1 so the diffuser and intake moved forward 1.9 mm.

nodes.label: Spacer Washer 21.8/16 x1.5
nodes.rationale: Bears on the outer ring only; ID 16 clears the inner ring (a 9 mm ID spacer would rub). Removed in v12.

nodes.label: Supply Lines Through Diffuser Vanes 1/5/9
nodes.rationale: 3 mm brass lines replace 3 of the 13 vane screws, as on the GR130 diffuser.

nodes.label: v11 Changes: Sensors, Igniter, Rotor Clamp
nodes.norm_label: v11 changes: sensors, igniter, rotor clamp

nodes.label: v12 Changes: Threads, Oil-Feed Rings, O-ring
nodes.norm_label: v12 changes: threads, oil-feed rings, o-ring

nodes.label: Vaporiser Sticks (12 straight, 6 mm)
nodes.rationale: GR180 photo 'Combustion chamber 5' shows 12 straight sticks, overriding the GR130 J-shape; fixed in the front cap in v9.

nodes.label: Left-Hand M6x1 Shaft-End Threads
nodes.rationale: Rotor turns CCW seen from the intake (backswept exducer), so LH threads make the nose cone tighten under starter torque and the turbine nut tighten under air drag; all other threads are RH.

nodes.label: Wave Spring Bearing Preload (~15 N)
nodes.rationale: Single-turn wave spring (t 0.2-0.25, free 3.0, installed 2.8) gives ~15 N axial preload, adjusted by grinding the spacer; in v12 it sits at x9.1-11.3.

nodes.label: C3: Turbine Tip Clearance Only 0.10 mm
nodes.norm_label: c3: turbine tip clearance only 0.10 mm
nodes.rationale: 0.2-0.3 mm is usually needed for a 70 mm wheel at 120k rpm given thermal and centrifugal growth.

nodes.label: C4: Turbine Centred on Only 7.7 mm of 8 mm Seat
nodes.norm_label: c4: turbine centred on only 7.7 mm of 8 mm seat
nodes.rationale: Shaft 8 mm seat ends at x=115 while the hub runs to x=121.8, so 6.8 mm of bore sits on the M6 thread (caused by the v11 6.3 spacer); weakens centring and balance repeatability. Move thread start to >=122 with a longer shaft, or shorten the hub.

nodes.label: ECU Control and Safety Systems
nodes.rationale: ECU with speed governor and EGT limiter, two gas shut-off valves, flame detection, burst containment and a test stand.

nodes.label: I3: 1.4 mm Unshrouded Turbine Tip Trailing Edge
nodes.norm_label: i3: 1.4 mm unshrouded turbine tip trailing edge

nodes.label: I8: Rotor Stress and Burst Containment
nodes.norm_label: i8: rotor stress and burst containment
nodes.rationale: 442 m/s turbine tip speed is normal for model engines but continuous duty needs de-rating (lower speed and TIT) and mandatory burst containment.

nodes.label: P1: Hard-Coded Output Path
nodes.rationale: OUT=~/Desktop/GR180-3D in build, verify, _v12 scripts and GR180Tools means running the build from this backup overwrites the main folder, which has already diverged (v13).

nodes.label: P4: Magic Numbers, No Shared Params File
nodes.norm_label: p4: magic numbers, no shared params file

nodes.label: 608 Hybrid Ceramic Bearings (2x)
nodes.rationale: User-selected 8x22x7 Si3N4-ball ABEC-7 full-complement / 15 deg angular-contact bearings (e.g. GRW D608/602839) for high-speed rotor support.

nodes.label: NGV (GR180_NGV, 15 vanes)
nodes.rationale: 15 vanes per NGV70blank; the sheet's 16 deg is the trailing-edge line (not modelled) and the 68/64 deg exit angle is assumed.

nodes.label: Rear Stack Spacer 12/8 x6.3
nodes.rationale: Added in v11 between the shaft shoulder (x94) and the rear 608 inner ring so the turbine nut clamp closes, with the shaft lengthened 4.8 mm for 6 mm nut engagement.

nodes.label: GR180 Shaft
nodes.rationale: Bearing seats 8 mm -0.002/-0.005 and 7 mm sections +0.005 taken from the GR130 shaft sheet; shoulder moved to x60.1 in v12.

nodes.label: Turbine (GR180_Turbine 70.3 mm, 23 blades)
nodes.rationale: Blade count from the TW70 front view; front sleeve 13x6, dished web and blade angles are assumed.

nodes.label: Turbine Nut Thread Engagement Only 2.2 mm
nodes.norm_label: turbine nut thread engagement only 2.2 mm
nodes.rationale: Shaft thread runs to x=124 and the drawing implies the rear bearing sits ~6 mm further forward; flagged unresolved in v8.

nodes.label: Architecture A: PM Generator on Core Shaft
nodes.norm_label: architecture a: pm generator on core shaft
nodes.rationale: Rejected: needs a new turbine (loading 1.17 to 1.6), generator mass moves the critical speed to 118-127k rpm, and the environment is hot.

nodes.label: Architecture B: Free Power Turbine + Two-Stage Gearbox
nodes.norm_label: architecture b: free power turbine + two-stage gearbox
nodes.rationale: 20-23:1 reduction from 60-70k rpm to 3000 rpm needs a ground high-speed pinion with jet lubrication, but allows a standard 50 Hz generator without inverter.

nodes.label: Architecture C: FPT + High-Speed PM Generator + Inverter
nodes.norm_label: architecture c: fpt + high-speed pm generator + inverter
nodes.rationale: Mechanically simple: an RC/EV-class high-speed BLDC acts as generator and complexity moves into the electronics; recommended for the first prototype.

nodes.label: C2: Bending/Conical Mode Near Operating Speed
nodes.norm_label: c2: bending/conical mode near operating speed
nodes.rationale: Third forward critical speed lies at 110-126k rpm, within +/-20% of the operating speed; stiffnesses are engineering estimates, so tap test the rotor, keep the front O-ring damper and add no mass to the shaft.

nodes.label: C5: Bearing Life for Generator Duty
nodes.norm_label: c5: bearing life for generator duty
nodes.rationale: 608 at 120k rpm reaches n*dm ~1.8e6; with total-loss lubrication model-engine life is tens of hours versus hundreds to thousands for a generator.

nodes.label: Generator Conversion Options
nodes.rationale: ~300 kW fuel input, ~37 kW jet kinetic energy; simple-cycle electrical efficiency 6-8% versus 25-35% for piston gas gensets; 10-18 kW electrical is realistic for a first prototype.

nodes.label: GR180 Single-Spool 180 N Turbojet
nodes.rationale: 37 parts built parametrically in FreeCAD; design speed ~120k rpm (compressor tip 465 m/s, turbine tip 442 m/s); rotor mass 337 g with bearing span 98.2 mm.

nodes.label: Recuperated Cycle (eff. 0.85, ~15%)
nodes.rationale: Large heat exchanger raises combustor inlet air to 550 C, so the combustor must be redesigned.

nodes.label: GR180 Full Analysis and v12 Design Review
nodes.norm_label: gr180 full analysis and v12 design review

nodes.label: Free Power Turbine (FPT)
nodes.rationale: Recommended path: GR180 core stays untouched, the FPT NGV is sized to the current nozzle so the operating point is unchanged, and the new FPT shaft can use larger, longer-life bearings. Choose B for direct 50 Hz, otherwise C is simpler and cheaper.
